prompt.context_jp: 夜の営業部にはもう人影がなく、モニターの光だけ___机の並びに冷たく落ちていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: モニターの光だけ___机の並びに冷たく落ちていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits after 「モニターの光だけ」.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is introducing the lone remaining light as newly-seen information in the scene. 「だけが」 marks this as the single thing that stands out — an exhaustive-listing/new-info use of が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn 'only the monitor light' into a topic for comment, which is awkward here where the scene is being described from scratch. を doesn't fit the intransitive 落ちる.

contrast_examples.en: That light was cold. (topic known already)

prompt.context_jp: 朱雀の視線は、少し離れた席で軽やかに雑談を交わす若手たちに向いていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 朱雀の視線___、少し離れた席で軽やかに雑談を交わす若手たちに向いていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「朱雀の視線」.

feedback.correct_en: Suzaku has just been introduced; now the narrator shifts to his gaze as the topic, commenting on where it was directed. は marks that familiar topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present his gaze as brand-new information, as if we didn't just establish him. に doesn't fit a subject slot.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の視線は若手に向いていた。
contrast_examples.en: His gaze was on the youngsters. (topic)

contrast_examples.jp: 誰かの視線が刺さった。

prompt.context_jp: キーを叩く指の動きが以前より格段になめらかで、その几帳面な打鍵音だけ___静かに響いている。
prompt.prompt_jp: その几帳面な打鍵音だけ___静かに響いている。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「打鍵音だけ」.

feedback.correct_en: 'Only the keystroke sound' is being exhaustively singled out as what resonates in the silence — classic 〜だけが.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would contrast the sound against something else as topic, which doesn't match the scene-painting intent.

contrast_examples.jp: それだけは言わないで。
contrast_examples.en: Just don't say that one thing. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: フロアの奥から、鴫石部長___真っ直ぐこちらへ歩いてくる足音が近づいてきた。
prompt.prompt_jp: フロアの奥から、鴫石部長___真っ直ぐこちらへ歩いてくる足音が近づいてきた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「鴫石部長」.

feedback.correct_en: Shigiishi is appearing on the scene as new information inside a relative clause (「真っ直ぐこちらへ歩いてくる」 modifies 足音). Subjects inside relative clauses typically take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は can't normally mark the subject of a relative clause here. The sentence introduces Shigiishi's arrival, not a comment about him as a topic.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が歩いてくる音がした。
contrast_examples.en: The sound of him walking came.

prompt.context_jp: 早く帰ると家族___嫌な顔をする
prompt.prompt_jp: 早く帰ると家族___嫌な顔をする
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「家族」 in Suzaku's recalled line.

feedback.correct_en: Inside a 〜と conditional clause describing what happens, the subject is new/neutral information: が. The family's reaction is the event being reported.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'the family' a contrastive topic ('as for the family...'), which clashes with the hypothetical conditional reading.

contrast_examples.jp: 雨が降ると道が濡れる。
contrast_examples.en: When it rains, the road gets wet.

prompt.context_jp: 時計の針___、まだ夜と呼ぶには早い時間を指していた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 時計の針___、まだ夜と呼ぶには早い時間を指していた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「時計の針」.

feedback.correct_en: The clock has been in view throughout this scene (「ダッシュボードの時計を見つめる」). Now the narrator comments on it as the established topic — は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would reintroduce the clock hand as fresh information, which doesn't match the continuing reflection.

prompt.context_jp: 経済が上向く予感の中で、彼ら___まだ何にでも成れる気でいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼ら___まだ何にでも成れる気でいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「彼ら」.

feedback.correct_en: The young Suzaku and co. have already been established; the narrator is now making a general comment about them as the topic — は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present them as new information in a specific event, but this is a reflective, atemporal statement.

prompt.context_jp: 昔 クライアントに 蹴り飛ばされたとき かばってくれたの___ 朱雀さんだし
prompt.prompt_jp: かばってくれたの___ 朱雀さんだし
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle in Hatoyama's sentimental line.

feedback.correct_en: This is a classic cleft/identification: 'The one who protected me was Suzaku.' Exhaustive-listing が picks out Suzaku as THE person.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would reverse the information structure ('As for the one who protected me...'), which is possible but less natural; the speaker is singling Suzaku out.

contrast_examples.jp: 助けてくれたのが先生だ。
contrast_examples.en: The one who saved me was the teacher.

prompt.context_jp: キッチンからは、妻の亜矢子___振り向くこともなく皿を洗う背中が見えた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 妻の亜矢子___振り向くこともなく皿を洗う背中が見えた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「亜矢子」.

feedback.correct_en: Ayako is the subject inside a relative clause modifying 背中 ('the back of Ayako, who was washing dishes...'). Relative-clause subjects take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は generally cannot mark the subject within a relative clause.

contrast_examples.jp: 子供が遊ぶ声が聞こえる。

prompt.context_jp: 食べたことに 怒ってるんじゃないの 食べてから“ごめんね”って 言わないから怒ってんの！
prompt.prompt_jp: 食べたこと___ 怒ってるんじゃないの
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「食べたこと」.

feedback.correct_en: 怒る takes に to mark the thing one is angry about. Kana is saying she isn't angry AT the fact of him eating it — but at his failure to apologize.
feedback.incorrect_en: を doesn't pair with 怒る. が would mark a subject, not the object of anger.

contrast_examples.en: To get angry at rude behavior.

prompt.context_jp: それって あなた___ 毎日 家にいるってことでしょう？
prompt.prompt_jp: あなた___ 毎日 家にいるってことでしょう？
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「あなた」 in the embedded clause.

feedback.correct_en: Inside the こと-clause ('the fact that you are home every day'), あなた is the subject of a subordinate clause → が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside a こと/ってこと embedded clause normally shifts to が unless strongly contrastive. Here the wife is defining what retirement MEANS, not contrasting him.

prompt.context_jp: IT機器___、彼にとって昔から根本的に苦手なものだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: IT機器___、彼にとって昔から根本的に苦手なものだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「IT機器」.

feedback.correct_en: 'IT equipment' is being set up as the topic for a general evaluative comment (苦手だった). Characteristic 〜は〜が苦手 pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark it as the subject in a neutral-description event, but this is clearly a topic-comment generalization.

contrast_examples.en: Math is what I'm bad at. (identificational)

prompt.context_jp: 顔を上げた先には、いつもと同じ制服姿の鷹野___立っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: いつもと同じ制服姿の鷹野___立っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「鷹野」.

feedback.correct_en: Suzaku looks up and Takano appears as newly-perceived information — classic が of 'discovery'.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make Takano a known topic, but the point is that he's just now noticing her presence.

prompt.context_jp: お礼ぐらい… 昔のあなた___ ちゃんと言えたはずだと思いますが
prompt.prompt_jp: 昔のあなた___ ちゃんと言えたはず
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「昔のあなた」.

feedback.correct_en: なら sets up a contrastive hypothetical: 'If it were the old you, you could have said it.' Shigiishi is contrasting past Suzaku with the current one.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present 'old you' as a plain subject without the contrastive-conditional nuance that drives the whole scene.

contrast_examples.jp: 昔の彼なら許してくれた。
contrast_examples.en: The old him would have forgiven me.

prompt.context_jp: あなた___変わりました あのころ いちばん なりたくなかった人間に 今なってると思います
prompt.prompt_jp: あなた___変わりました
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「あなた」.

feedback.correct_en: Shigiishi is making a direct comment ABOUT Suzaku as the topic of the whole speech: 'You, you've changed.' は.
feedback.incorrect_en: あなたが would sound like identifying who changed ('YOU are the one who changed'), as if answering a question — not the accusatory topic-comment Shigiishi delivers.

contrast_examples.jp: あなたが変わったのね。
contrast_examples.en: So YOU're the one who changed.

prompt.context_jp: 彼はそっと頭___手をやり、指先で薄くなった生え際を確かめた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼はそっと頭___手をやり
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「頭」.

feedback.correct_en: 手をやる means 'to put/send a hand to' a location → に marks the destination.
feedback.incorrect_en: 頭を手にやる doesn't make sense. で would mark a place of action, not the target of the motion.

contrast_examples.en: To put a hand to one's mouth.
To work at the desk. (location of action)

prompt.context_jp: “クライアントは 飲ませて 食わせて ___”が 合言葉だったからね
prompt.prompt_jp: クライアントは 飲ませて 食わせて ___
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits the old sales motto?

feedback.correct_en: 落とす in sales slang means 'to close/land' a client. The slogan is 'wine them, dine them, close them.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 倒す ('defeat') and 消す ('erase') don't carry the 'win over / close a deal' nuance of 落とす here.

prompt.context_jp: いやいや いやいや… ___ よだつ話にしか 聞こえないけど
prompt.prompt_jp: ___ よだつ話にしか 聞こえないけど
prompt.prompt_en: Fill the blank in the idiom meaning 'hair-raising / horrifying'.

feedback.correct_en: 身の毛もよだつ is a set idiom for 'blood-curdling / makes one's hair stand on end.'
feedback.incorrect_en: The other options are not real idioms; the fixed phrase requires 身の毛.

contrast_examples.en: The blood drains from one's face. (different idiom)

prompt.context_jp: そこから 2人で___に 暮らすんじゃなかったのか？
prompt.prompt_jp: 2人で___に 暮らす
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word Suzaku uses for a leisurely retired life.

feedback.correct_en: 悠々自適 is the standard four-character compound for 'living a comfortable, leisurely life (esp. in retirement).'
feedback.incorrect_en: 自由奔放 means 'free-spirited/wild,' not quite the retirement nuance. 一期一会 is 'once-in-a-lifetime encounter.'

contrast_examples.en: After retirement, I'll live at ease.

prompt.context_jp: 朱雀は思わず、___にもすがるような目で彼女を見上げた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ___にもすがるような目で
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the idiom meaning 'desperate / grasping at straws.'

feedback.correct_en: 藁にもすがる is the fixed idiom — 'to clutch even at straws' when desperate.
feedback.incorrect_en: The idiom is set with 藁 (straw); other nouns don't form this expression.

contrast_examples.en: Desperate enough to grasp at straws.
To be blown by the wind. (unrelated)

prompt.context_jp: こっち___下手に出れば 案外 話せるヤツかもしれん
prompt.prompt_jp: こっちが___に出れば
prompt.prompt_en: Fill the blank: 'if I act humble/take a low posture.'

feedback.correct_en: 下手に出る (したてにでる) means 'to take a humble/deferential attitude.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 上手に出る isn't a set phrase in this sense; 前に出る means 'to step forward,' not 'to be humble.'

prompt.context_jp: こういう所が ___ だって言われるんだ 我慢 我慢
prompt.prompt_jp: こういう所が ___ だって言われるんだ
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in: 'this is why I get called a ___.'

feedback.correct_en: 老害 ('harmful old person / out-of-touch elder') is a well-known modern buzzword that fits Suzaku's self-aware worry.
feedback.incorrect_en: 若害 isn't a standard word; 災害 means 'disaster' in the sense of natural calamities.

contrast_examples.jp: 老害と言われたくない。
contrast_examples.en: I don't want to be called an out-of-touch old man.

prompt.context_jp: 何かしてもらったら___ 迷惑をかけたら“ごめんなさい”
prompt.prompt_jp: 何かしてもらったら___
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the expected polite response.

feedback.correct_en: Paired with ごめんなさい for apology, ありがとう is the thanks half of this basic etiquette pair the whole chapter builds toward.
feedback.incorrect_en: すみません can mean sorry OR thanks but doesn't contrast cleanly with ごめんなさい here. いただきます is said before eating.

contrast_examples.jp: 助けてくれてありがとう。

prompt.context_jp: 営業部全員の社内チャットに とんでもない文章を ___ してしまいました！
prompt.prompt_jp: とんでもない文章を ___ してしまいました
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the slang verb for 'misfire a message to the wrong group.'

feedback.correct_en: 誤爆する ('mis-bomb') is slang for accidentally sending a message to the wrong chat/person.
feedback.incorrect_en: 誤発 isn't standard here; 誤報 means 'false report' (news), not a chat misfire.

contrast_examples.en: I sent a LINE message to the wrong chat.

prompt.context_jp: On a holiday Takano greets Suzaku at the office.
prompt.prompt_en: Which greeting sounds most natural coming from Takano to her boss first thing in the morning at the office?

choices.text: 部長 おはようございます

feedback.correct_en: おはようございます is the standard first-encounter-of-the-day office greeting regardless of actual time.
feedback.incorrect_en: こんにちは is unusual between coworkers inside the office. どうも alone is too casual for addressing one's boss.

contrast_examples.en: Thanks for your work. (later in the day)

prompt.context_jp: Suzaku awkwardly thanks his wife and she reacts.
prompt.prompt_en: Which reaction best captures the wife's startled 'ugh, that's creepy' tone in casual spoken Japanese?

choices.text: はい、気持ちが悪いです

feedback.correct_en: はぁ？ 気持ち悪い is the natural blunt casual reaction — exactly what she says in the story.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is ungrammatical as a reaction. C is overly polite and misses the dismissive emotion the scene calls for.

prompt.context_jp: Suzaku asks Takano to call someone for him.
prompt.prompt_en: Which of these is the most natural, polite workplace reply to a boss's request?

feedback.correct_en: かしこまりました is formal 'certainly / understood' — exactly Takano's reply and typical business etiquette.
feedback.incorrect_en: 分かる and いいよ are casual and inappropriate when addressing one's boss.

prompt.context_jp: Suzaku forces himself to thank Hiwada for working on his day off.
prompt.prompt_en: Which rendering best captures Suzaku's halting, awkward 'thank you' in this emotional moment?

choices.text: ハァ… あり… がとう
どうもありがとうございました、本当に。

feedback.correct_en: The broken, drawn-out delivery with pauses matches a man who struggles enormously to say the word — the chapter's emotional climax.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is too fluent and polished for someone who has never apologized before. C (English loanword) would undercut the gravity.

contrast_examples.jp: ありがとうございます。

prompt.context_jp: Shigiishi (via phone, posing as 'MOZU') asks to add a word.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing is the most natural polite way to interject 'May I say one thing?' in a workplace call?

choices.text: ひと言 よろしいですか？
ひと言 言っていい？
ひと言 しゃべらせろ

feedback.correct_en: ひと言よろしいですか is the standard polite phrase for cutting into a conversation respectfully.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is casual and inappropriate between coworkers in this formal register. C is a rude imperative.

contrast_examples.jp: ひと言よろしいでしょうか。
